reading_decisions.why: Its split between user-driven redirection (E04/E08/E12) and uncorrected mechanical failure (E02/E06/E10) matches the frozen record and it names its own counterevidence, though 'high' confidence outruns a 12-episode synthetic sample.

Its broader claim that failed and unknown episodes create a remediation need goes beyond any recorded correction, but it flags that limit explicitly, preserves unknown as unknown, and refuses to call the changed-decision episodes agent errors.
Its strict claim that the [correction] line appears only in changed-decision episodes is exactly what the corpus shows, and it surfaces E04 and E12 as the right complications to its own codes.

output.what_changed_my_view: The A/C versus B disagreement over whether failed or unknown results 'require correction' pushed me to split the answer: recorded corrections track only human redirection of target, scope, or visibility, while failed/unknown episodes carry an unmet, unrecorded correction need the corpus cannot adjudicate. E12 (all-succeeded yet corrected) and E04 (failed edit plus correction) confirmed that correction is decoupled from tool-outcome status.
